title: Threat Hunting Analyst /Information Technology Specialist 3 (Information Security), ref 5774M-10BR

cond_0001.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, the incumbent will be a Threat Hunting Analyst working in the Security Operations Center. The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.
This position requires the incumbent to possess a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Duties Include, But Are Not Limited To
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets
Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings
Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA), Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI), Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO).
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst, Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs), Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations, Participating in cyber incident response.

Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology, and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls)
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting, including the ability to articulate information technology and information security concepts to varied audiences
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving, and analytical skills

Certifications in one or more of the following:
Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA)
Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI)
Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO)
1+ Years of experience in one or more of the following:
Working as a SOC analyst
Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs)
Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations
Participating in cyber incident response

cond_0080.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within [Company name masked], you will serve as a Threat Hunting Analyst in the Security Operations Center. You will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to execute both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. You will take ownership of ingesting and responding to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other open-source intelligence sources.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires you to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.
cond_0080.responsibilities:
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings
Execute threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets
Lead responses to ad-hoc requests, research, and threat hunts, and direct support to other business units as needed
Drive the creation of detection content based on threat hunting findings
Document all threat hunts, track findings, and build trends from results
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain
Produce daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs
Deliver technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events
Take ownership of active projects to identify and resolve issues and ensure successful outcomes
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned

cond_0126.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within [Company name masked], you will work as a Threat Hunting Analyst in the Security Operations Center. You will coordinate with the team to leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to support both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. You will also work alongside colleagues to help process and respond to threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other open-source intelligence sources.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to help identify and contain potential cyber threats. The role also involves working with a degree of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0126.responsibilities:
Coordinate with the team to monitor and report on current and emerging threats, including exploitable vulnerabilities and their details
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all-source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs, and warnings
Work alongside colleagues to perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to help ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats
Help identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets
Respond to ad-hoc requests and research, support threat hunts, and assist other business units as needed
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings
Document all threat hunts, track findings, and help create trends based on results
Classify and categorize hunting use cases based on the MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain
Contribute to daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs
Help create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues and ensure successful outcomes
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned
cond_0126.requirements:
Bachelor's degree* with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience**.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Certifications in one or more of the following:
Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA)
Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI)
Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO)
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following:
Working as a SOC analyst
Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs)
Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations
Participating in cyber incident response
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.

Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology, and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls)
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting, including the ability to articulate information technology and information security concepts to varied audiences

Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA)
Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI)
Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO)
1+ Years of experience in one or more of the following:
Working as a SOC analyst
Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs)
Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations
Participating in cyber incident response

cond_0134.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within [Company name masked], you will serve as a Threat Hunting Analyst in the Security Operations Center. You will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to execute both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. You will take ownership of ingesting and responding to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other open-source intelligence sources.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires you to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
Background check and fingerprinting are required.
cond_0134.responsibilities:
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings
Execute threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets
Lead responses to ad-hoc requests, research, and threat hunts, and direct support to other business units as needed
Drive the creation of detection content based on threat hunting findings
Document all threat hunts, track findings, and build trends from results
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain
Produce daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs
Deliver technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events
Take ownership of active projects to identify and resolve issues and ensure successful outcomes
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned

cond_0194.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, the incumbent will be a Threat Hunting Analyst working in the Security Operations Center. The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.

The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.
This position requires the incumbent to possess a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with threat hunting and security operations work.
cond_0329.responsibilities:
Duties Include, But Are Not Limited To
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets
Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings
Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned
cond_0329.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following:
Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA)
Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI)
Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO)
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following:
Working as a SOC analyst
Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs)
Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations
Participating in cyber incident response

cond_0359.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within [Company name masked], you will serve as a Threat Hunting Analyst in the Security Operations Center. You will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to execute both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. You will take ownership of ingesting and responding to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other open-source intelligence sources.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires you to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0359.responsibilities:
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities
Lead research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings
Execute threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets
Respond to ad-hoc requests, research, threat hunts, and direct coordination with other business units as needed
Own the creation of detection content based on threat hunting findings
Document all threat hunts, track findings, and build trends based on results
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain
Deliver daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs
Produce technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events
Drive active projects to identify and resolve issues/problems and ensure successful outcomes are achieved
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned
cond_0359.requirements:
Bachelor's degree* with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience**.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA) Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI) Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO)
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs) Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations Participating in cyber incident response
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.

cond_0444.intro:
Under the direction of senior leadership within the Office of Information Technology Services, the incumbent will be a Threat Hunting Analyst working in the Security Operations Center. The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.
This position requires the incumbent to possess a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0444.responsibilities:
Duties Include, But Are Not Limited To
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets
Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings
Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned
cond_0444.requirements:
Education
Bachelor's degree in cyber security, information assurance, information technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Candidates with a bachelor's degree but fewer than 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology are welcome to apply with an additional year of general IT experience. Relevant information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree with an additional two years of general IT experience is also considered. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general IT experience requirement.
Experience
Around two years of information technology experience, including around one year of information security or information assurance experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Certifications
Background in one or more of the following certification areas is helpful; a willingness to obtain is also considered:
Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA)
Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI)
Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO)
Technical Experience
Around 1 year of experience in one or more of the following areas:
Working as a SOC analyst
Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs)
Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations
Participating in cyber incident response
Working knowledge of enterprise IT environments, including system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Familiarity with the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Soft Skills
Ability to communicate clearly in both oral and written form, including the ability to explain IT and information security concepts to varied audiences.
Willingness to think critically, work through problems analytically, and develop solutions over time.

Bachelor's degree with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
Preferred Requirements
Certifications in one or more of the following:
Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA)
Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI)
Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO)
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following:
Working as a SOC analyst
Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs)
Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations
Participating in cyber incident response

cond_0474.intro:
We are looking for a Threat Hunting Analyst to join our team.
Under the direction of senior leadership within [Company name masked], the incumbent will work in the Security Operations Center. The role involves leveraging a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. You will regularly connect with many third parties — such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other open-source intelligence sources — to stay current on threats and vulnerability announcements.
This position requires a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to quickly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. It also requires a high degree of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction.
cond_0474.responsibilities:
Duties include, but are not limited to:
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets
Respond to ad-hoc requests, research, threat hunts, and actively assist other business units as needed
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings
Document all threat hunts, track, and create trends based on the findings
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events — clearly communicating findings to both technical and non-technical audiences
Actively participate in projects to help identify and resolve issues and ensure successful outcomes
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned

The incumbent will leverage a variety of threat intelligence sources and indicators of compromise (IOCs) to perform both proactive and reactive threat hunting across a large and diverse multi-entity environment. The incumbent will participate in the ingestion and response to all forms of threat intelligence and vulnerability announcements received from many third parties such as vendors, DHS CISA, MS-ISAC, and other sources of open-source intelligence.
This position requires the incumbent to possess a solid understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, the tactics, techniques, tools, and procedures commonly leveraged, and the steps necessary to swiftly identify and contain a potential cyber threat. Additionally, this position requires an incumbent to act with a great deal of independence in alignment with agency and upper-level management strategic direction. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of threat hunting and how different pieces of intelligence connect.
cond_0535.responsibilities:
Monitor and report on current and emerging threats including exploitable vulnerabilities, and details of those vulnerabilities
Conduct research, analysis, and correlation across a wide variety of all source data sets such as IOCs, IOAs and warnings
Perform threat hunting across a multi-OS/multi-cloud environment to ensure a timely and effective response to new cyber threats
Identify tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) for intrusion sets
Respond to ad-hoc request, research, threat hunts, and assist with other business units as needed
Assist with creating detection content based on threat hunting findings
Document all threat hunt, track, and create trends based on the findings
Classify/categorize hunting use cases based on MITRE ATT&CK framework and cyber kill chain
Create daily, monthly, and yearly intelligence information in support of business needs
Create technical reports and executive summaries related to cyber security incidents and events
Participate in active projects to help identify and resolve issues/problems to ensure successful outcomes are achieved
Perform the full range of supervisory responsibilities, as assigned
cond_0535.requirements:
Bachelor's degree* with at least 15 credit hours in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology; and two years of information technology experience, including one year of information security or information assurance experience**.
Substitution: bachelor's degree candidates without at least 15 course credits in cyber security, information assurance, or information technology require an additional year of general information technology experience to qualify. Appropriate information security or information assurance experience may substitute for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis; an associate's degree requires an additional two years of general information technology experience. Experience solely in information security or information assurance may substitute for the general information technology experience.
Certifications in one or more of the following: Cyber Defense (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GCED, GSOM, GSOC, GMON, GCDA) Cyber Threat Intelligence (e.g., GCTI, CTIA, CCIP, GOSI) Information Security Management (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CCISO)
1+ Years' experience in one or more of the following: Working as a SOC analyst Conducting log analysis (e.g., firewall logs, DNS logs, proxy logs, IDS/IPS logs) Using SIEM technologies to support in-depth investigations Participating in cyber incident response
Strong understanding of enterprise IT environments, including but not limited to system administration, network architecture, operating systems, endpoint detection and response tools, and network-based security solutions (e.g., IDS/IPS, firewalls).
Strong understanding of the foundations of Information Security, such as the CIA triad, information classification, identity and access management, risk management, vulnerability management, secure architecture and engineering, network security, software development security, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to clearly articulate information technology and information security concepts to a varied audience to facilitate wide understanding.
Demonstrated critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.
